title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: shipping customers need predictable unit economics and reasonable out-of-the-box inference cost/latency tradeoffs. This PR introduces three coordinated features: 1) autotuned defaults for batching and KV caching that adapt to common request distributions; 2) quantization profile selection and metadata so the serving runtime can pick per-customer/route quant profiles; 3) a unit-economics (uecon) tooling integration in the Console and CLI that surfaces recommended config changes and estimated $/1K tokens impact. Changes are implemented as an iterative rollout with config flags and feature gates. Checklist: - [x] implement batching/autotune heuristics - [x] add persistent KV cache default policy - [x] quantization profile selection API + model metadata - [x] uecon estimator and console UI + CLI hook - [x] e2e tests for autotune logic - [x] docs and release notes - [x] rollout feature flag + telemetry to validate in staging Description of work: the autotune defaults module watches recent request latency and effective batch sizes and recommends (and can optionally apply) defaults for max_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, and cache_policies. We persist per-route defaults in the config store and expose a read-only preview in Console. Quantization profiles are added as model registry metadata; the runtime now exposes an ordered list of compatible quant profiles and a selection policy to prefer lower-precision profiles that pass quality thresholds. The unit-econ tooling computes an estimated cost delta for config changes (batching, caching, quant) using historical token distribution and GPU/instance unit cost. It displays the top-3 recommendations and estimated monthly savings. Rollout plan: feature gated, enabled for internal accounts in staging, then opt-in for small beta customers. Related: ENG-4821 (autotune), ENG-4890 (uecon), SUP-1203 (support ticket where customer requested clearer defaults).
